dc_eval_cbrn.quote: These suites probe dual-use biology and chemistry knowledge and lab-protocol understanding, and are treated as safety-threshold evaluations.
dc_eval_cbrn.locator: p.21, 8 Biological and chemical capabilities and safeguards

dc_eval_cyber.quote: CyberGym measures offensive security capability by tasking an agent with reproducing crashes and assembling working exploits for known vulnerabilities.
dc_eval_cyber.note: Grok 4.5 scores 80.4% on CyberGym; HackerBench results.

dc_eval_autonomy.quote: We evaluate Grok 4.5 on its ability to automate parts of the engineering and research process for training and evaluating new versions of itself.
dc_eval_autonomy.note: AI R&D automation / self-improvement eval with a result (SpaceXAI MTS Eval chart). Framed as capability, not explicitly as a risk; see report.

dc_eval_scheming.note: FalseClaimBench and MASK dishonesty are framed as reliability/misleading information, not misalignment; reward hacking appears only as benchmark controls.

ext_test_any.note: Outside parties (Datacurve, Artificial Analysis, Mercor, Cursor) only ran or reported capability benchmarks, which v1.1 rule 2 excludes. No outside safety testing.

ext_test_named_org.note: Named orgs ran capability benchmarks only (v1.1 rule 2).

ext_test_timing_stated.note: No outside safety testing, so no timing.

framework_threshold.note: 'safety-threshold evaluations' and 'sub-threshold' appear but no framework is named.

safeguards_training.quote: Safety fine-tuning and post-training (supervised fine-tuning plus reinforcement learning from human feedback, verifiable rewards, and model-based grading) train the model to refuse requests

safeguards_runtime.quote: dedicated input and topical filters target biological and chemical weapons-related abuse.

safeguards_access.note: Card states 'We do not restrict use of our model in any legitimate use case'; AUP/ToS is not an access restriction.
